stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category which has finite limits.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $n$ the functor $\text{sk}_n : \text{Simp}(\mathcal{C})
\to \text{Simp}_n(\mathcal{C})$ has a right adjoint $\text{cosk}_n$.
\item For every $n' \geq n$ the functor
$\text{sk}_n : \text{Simp}_{n'}(\mathcal{C}) \to \text{Simp}_n(\mathcal{C})$
has a right adjoint, namely $\text{sk}_{n'}\text{cosk}_n$.
\item For every $m \geq n \geq 0$ and every $n$-truncated simplicial
object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ we have
$\text{cosk}_m \text{sk}_m \text{cosk}_n U = \text{cosk}_n U$.
\item If $U$ is a simplicial object of $\mathcal{C}$ such that
the canonical map
$U \to \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_nU$
is an isomorphism for some $n \geq 0$, then the canonical map
$U \to \text{cosk}_m \text{sk}_mU$
is an isomorphism for all $m \geq n$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let C be a category with finite limits.
conclusions: For each n≥0 the restriction functor sk_n:Simp(C)→Simp_n(C) has right adjoint cosk_n.
For n'≥n≥0, sk_n:Simp_{n'}(C)→Simp_n(C) has right adjoint sk_{n'}cosk_n.
For m≥n≥0 and n-truncated U, cosk_m sk_m cosk_n U≅cosk_n U.
For a simplicial U with U→cosk_n sk_n U an isomorphism for some n≥0, the analogous canonical map U→cosk_m sk_m U is an isomorphism for every m≥n.

reason: The proof derives the right adjoints and truncated recovery directly from the prior coskeleton existence and inductive-coskeleton discussion, with the last claim a formal consequence.
